piezas.titular: GeoBreath guides breathing exercises with geometric shapes and an adjustable rhythm
piezas.entradilla: Luis Vilela Acuña's app uses an animated shape to show when to breathe in, hold and breathe out. It opens in the browser, with nothing to install, and is available in six languages.
cuerpo: GeoBreath is a guided-breathing web app created by Luis Vilela Acuña as part of the [EDUmind](pieza:2026-11-06/edumind-miclase-sincronizacion) set of tools. In the Vibe Coding Educativo resource repository it is listed under an AGPL v3 licence (the page adds the EUPL-1.2 option) and catalogued for nursery, primary, secondary, sixth form and adult education.

When opened, it shows a shape (circle, triangle, square, pentagon or hexagon) with a dot that travels along its sides. In the centre, a prompt (“Breathe in”, “Hold”, “Breathe out”) says which phase is under way. Each side corresponds to a count: the value can be set between 1 and 10 seconds and, in advanced mode, each phase can be given a different duration. The screen also shows the session time, the cycles completed and a 15-cycle challenge that can be reset.

As well as a free rhythm, it offers four preset patterns: resonance (about 5.5 breaths per minute), box breathing 4-4-4-4, 4-7-8 and the physiological sigh. There are also three quick routines, called “Calma rápida”, “Foco estudio” and “Recupero exprés”, each with its own shape, rhythm and support switched on. The sensory supports are sound, vibration, pictograms and voice, which are switched on separately; and a number of rounds can be set, after which the session stops by itself.

In class it could serve as a guided pause on coming back from break, before an exam or in a tutorial, projected on the board for the whole group. According to the page itself, settings are saved only on the device and can be deleted with a button.

The interface has a language selector offering Spanish, Galician, Catalan, Basque, English and Chinese. The page shows a link to EDUmind, but nothing suggests that an account is needed to breathe along with it. The code is open and is on [GitHub](https://github.com/edumind-es/geobreath).

piezas.titular: A web editor lets teachers design collectable fauna and flora cards for the classroom
piezas.entradilla: The Eco-Duel Card Generator, created by David Cordones, offers a form for composing cards with data on animals and plants, with one collection per school year, from the first year of primary to the second year of Bachillerato.
cuerpo: The [Generador de Cromos Eco-Duel](https://elcordones.github.io/generador_cromos/) is an editor that opens in the browser and shows a form on the left and, on the right, the card as it is being put together. According to the repository's entry, it is meant for creating teaching material in the form of collectable cards, summarising concepts or assessing knowledge in a playful way. The entry places it between primary education and teacher training, and its author is David Cordones.

The form asks for the type of card (fauna or flora), the name, a group or subtitle (mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, fish, insect and others, in the case of fauna) and an image uploaded from the device. Values such as size and speed are then set with sliders, along with the trophic level (from producer to super-predator), rarity, diet, habitat, activity (diurnal, nocturnal…) and a curious fact. Each card is also assigned to a collection, which can be a school year, from the first year of primary to the second year of sixth form and basic vocational training, or a custom option, and carries a number.

In class, the tool lends itself to students making their own cards after researching a species, or to teachers preparing a collection for a game comparing characteristics in natural sciences. The interface can be switched between Catalan, Spanish and English, and the example it shows on opening, a wild boar, is in Catalan. Under the card there are two buttons, “Descarregar” and “Copiar”; the page does not say in what format it downloads or what is copied.

On opening the page, no registration or login is visible. The footer states that the code is licensed under AGPL v3 and the contents under CC BY-SA 4.0, which matches the licence declared in the repository's entry.

Título, autoría, licencia, ficha y archivo de la captura coinciden con la entrada. No se ha probado la descarga ni la copia. No hay enlaces a lo ya publicado. Los otros dos candidatos no se han elegido y no se descartan.
